steps.title: Open Main.java
steps.say: Time to run some code. Press **Ctrl+P**, type `Main` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders. Click somewhere in the editor first, so it hears your keys.

steps.title: A program
steps.say: This is Java. You don't need to understand all of it yet. Here's just the part that matters today.

marks.label: print a line of words in the terminal
the words to print, inside quote marks
every instruction ends with a semicolon

steps.title: Add your name
steps.say: Replace the three dots `...` with your name. Keep the quote marks, and don't remove the semicolon at the end. Then press **Ctrl+S** to save.

waitFor.hint: replace the dots with your name.

steps.title: Run it
steps.say: Click the **Run** button (▷) at the top right of the file. The output appears in the terminal at the bottom.

waitFor.hint: run the program and read the output.

steps.title: Read the output
steps.say: Your words appear in the terminal at the bottom. That's your program talking. If you see an error instead, read the first line: it usually says which line is wrong. A missing quote or semicolon is the most common reason.

steps.title: Check your work
steps.say: Press **Verify** in the lesson chip. It runs your program and checks it says your name.
